fields.name: Position
fields.evidence: Live: world coordinates (x 45..263, y 0.64..17, z -415..208) - the listener's position used to pick nearby subgrids. Windows: the SubgridProximity update part bg3.exe+0x771100 takes listeners with stride 0x40 and compares floats +0 and +8 (x, z) with the entity's current position (re-evaluates when moved by >= 1 m); the creator bg3.exe+0x77ADA0 zeroes +0..+0xB (8 + 4 bytes).

fields.name: _PadC
fields.evidence: Padding before the 8-aligned HashSet: the creator bg3.exe+0x77ADA0 writes +0..+0xB and +0x10..+0x3F but never +0xC, and no reader touches it; live values (0, 0xFFFFFFFF, others) are uninitialised memory.

fields.name: Subgrids
fields.evidence: Live: buckets ptr + 0x25..0x61 at +0x10, NextIds ptr/capacity 0x20|0x40/size at +0x20, Keys ptr/capacity/size 0x18..0x27 at +0x30 (a 48-byte HashSet). SubgridProximitySystem CommitFrameData (bg3.exe+0x771F30) walks each listener's 4-byte subgrid ids and counts them into SubgridProximityListComponent - hence 4-byte keys. Windows: creator bg3.exe+0x77ADA0 zeroes the 48 bytes; destructor bg3.exe+0x6B62A0 frees keys (+0x30), next-ids (+0x20) and buckets (+0x10); bg3.exe+0x771100 passes listener+0x10 to bg3.exe+0x772F70, which copies the set's keys (pointer +0x20, count +0x2C of the set) 4 bytes each - uint32_t subgrid ids.

open_questions: Names are ours; the meaning of the subgrid ids (aigrid subgrid indices) is from the system, not from a game name.
second_pass: Confirmed on Windows: creator bg3.exe+0x77ADA0 (vec3 zeroed, +0xC skipped, 48-byte set zeroed), destructor bg3.exe+0x6B62A0, and the update bg3.exe+0x771100 / bg3.exe+0x772F70 (position floats at +0/+8, set keys copied 4 bytes each). +0xC turned out to be padding, not a field.
